newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Aerospatiale flies back to the black.
newsitem.headline: French Aerospatiale flies back to the black.

text.p: French state-owned aerospace group Aerospatiale, in merger talks with fighter plane maker Dassault Aviation, said on Wednesday it had returned to profit in the first half of the year.

In a statement the company said it had posted a net profit of 273 million francs ($53 million) in the first six months of 1996 against a loss of 105 million in the first half of last year and a total 1995 loss of 981 million.

"We are seeing the first positive results of the company's restructuring plan of which the execution has started begin 1996 and of which the full effects will be felt at the end of 1998," the company said in a statement.
It said it had also benefited from a reduction in financial charges as wll as from a currency hedging policy which had allowed it to limit the effect of the dollar fall.
Its financial debts was cut by 2.9 billion francs to 3.6 billion francs, or 83 percent of shareholders funds.

Aerospatiale said the rest if the year depended on the dollar exchange rate, but nevertheless it was confident that the full year results, at unchanged dollar rates, would be in line with the increase seen in the first half.
"After this horizon, the company continues to apply its plans rigourously in order to be durably profitable even in an environment where the dollar is worth five francs," it said.
It said its new orders were 23.3 billion francs at the end of June 1996 against 20.4 billion at the end of the first half in 1995 and 39.3 billion for the full year.

At August 31, the new orders had reached 39.3 billion francs of which 23.3 billion for the aerospace branch, 1.9 billion for missiles, 4.8 billion for space and defence and 8.5 billion for helicopters.
It said this gave reason to expect new orders in 1996 which would be largerly superior than its sales figures.

Its first half sales were down to 23.11 billion francs from 24.63 billion in the first half of 1995. But Aerospatiale said that the decline was not sighificant and it expected full year 1996 sales to be at around the same level as the 1995 full year figure of 49.23 billion francs.
Aerospatiale, since August headed by Yves Michot after Louis Gallois moved to head railways group SNCF, is a 38 percent shareholder in civil plane maker Airbus Industrie. ($1=5.151 French Franc)
